title: Anchor-based offsetless pagination: monotonic anchors and consistency windows
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: Current dashboard APIs rely heavily on cursor-offset hybrids and large client-side scroll state which causes two recurring issues: (1) tail latency spikes when scans traverse hot shards using offset math and (2) correctness anomalies during concurrent writes/backfills where cursors point to shifting sequences. Goal: design and implement an anchor-based, offsetless pagination API for the Console Query service that provides stable monotonic anchors and configurable consistency windows to bound staleness, reduce read amplification, and simplify client state.

High-level approach: introduce a monotonic anchor token returned with each page. Anchors encode a compact snapshot marker (tenant-aware logical time plus an index shard hint) rather than an absolute offset. The backend will support three consistency modes: sticky (stable snapshot until page chain completes), bounded-window (allow up to N seconds of drift, controlled via request param), and live (best-effort read with hedging). The pagination plan will use: shard-aware anchor routing, lightweight anchor-to-index mapping cache with TTL, and optional snapshot backfill for long-lived anchor chains.

Key components to build:
- API layer: new endpoints /v2/dashboards/:id/rows/anchor_paginate that accept anchor token, page_size, consistency_mode, relay_hints. New response envelope includes next_anchor, anchor_ttl, snapshot_age_ms.
- Anchor encoder/decoder: deterministic, compact base64 tokens containing tenant id, sequence watermark, shard hint, and a small HMAC for integrity.
- Anchor routing: query router uses shard hint to route to preferred reader replica, falling back to cross-shard merge if hint mismatch.
- Anchor cache: LRU TTL cache mapping anchor->materialized index cursor. On cache miss, derive cursor from latest index snapshot + correction window. Cache entries are tenant-scoped and eviction-aware.
- Snapshot backfill: for anchor chains older than backfill_threshold, trigger opportunistic MVCC snapshotting on the hot shard to preserve monotonic reads. Backfill work is rate-limited and honors tenant quotas.
- Read hedging & hedging policy: for latency-sensitive queries, send parallel reads to 2 replicas and accept the first consistent result according to mode.
- Migration: keep old cursor API available; translator layer converts prior cursors to anchors for non-long-lived cursors.

Trade-offs and concerns:
- Pros: eliminates heavy offset scans, reduces tail latency, smaller client state (single token vs cursor list), explicit control of staleness and cost, easier correctness guarantees for concurrent writes.
- Cons: more complex server state for anchor mapping and backfill logic, added cache complexity and possible increase in memory, risk of stale anchors requiring careful TTL tuning.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Latency: 95th percentile query latency for paginated dashboard queries reduced by >=20% in pilot tenants.
- Cost: reduced number of read ops per page by >=15% compared to current offset-based scans.
- Correctness: zero data duplication or missing rows for monotonic anchor chains in sticky mode across 2-week smoke test.
- Operational: under 5% of anchor cache misses leading to backfill on production pilot traffic after tuning.

Compatibility and SDK changes:
- Console JS/Go SDKs need to support anchor token, expose consistency_mode flag, and auto-translate legacy cursor tokens when present. Add helper to persist short-lived anchors.

Rollout plan:
1) Design doc and proto API review (complete).
2) Implement anchor encoder/decoder + API surface behind feature flag (Ravi).
3) Anchor cache and router changes with unit/integration tests; iterate on TTL heuristics in staging (3 days).
4) Pilot rollout to two internal tenants and one small external customer with telemetry and anomaly alerts (2 weeks).
5) Measure metrics and expand rollout with canary percentages, enabling backfill slowly.
6) Deprecate legacy cursor endpoints after successful rollout and SDK updates (90 days notice).

Security and data protection:
- Anchors are HMAC-signed and include no raw PII; tenant scoping enforced server-side.
- Review requested for security team prior to enabling external pilot.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Finish encoder integration and unit tests (2 days).
- Implement anchor-to-cursor cache and basic eviction policy (3 days).
- Add integration tests verifying monotonicity across concurrent writes and backfills (3 days).
